facts.statement: Hypercubic describes its product Hopper as an "agentic TN3270 terminal emulator" that uses AI agents to navigate and operate inside mainframe z/OS environments.
facts.value: Agentic TN3270 terminal emulator leveraging AI agents to operate inside mainframes

facts.statement: Hopper is designed for z/OS engineers to help them navigate ISPF, write column-strict JCL, debug failed jobs, and query VSAM datasets using AI agents in a modern development environment.
facts.value: z/OS engineers aid for mainframe navigation, JCL, debugging, and querying

facts.statement: Hypercubic claims Hopper is the first agentic development environment for mainframes, combining TN3270 terminal, datasets and jobs browsers, and an AI agent capable of operating across multiple mainframe subsystems.
facts.value: First agentic development environment for mainframes

facts.statement: Hopper runs entirely on the user's laptop and connects to the mainframe over standard TN3270 and optional FTP protocols without requiring any installation on the mainframe itself.
facts.value: Client-side application connecting via TN3270 and FTP, no mainframe installation

facts.statement: Hopper depends on the existence of standard mainframe protocols TN3270 (required) and FTP (optional but recommended) to connect and operate within z/OS environments.
facts.value: Depends on TN3270 (required) and FTP (optional) mainframe protocols

bullets.text: Hypercubic is co-founded by Aayush Naik and Sai Gurrapu, as stated on the company website.
Sai Gurrapu is a co-founder of Hypercubic, according to the company website.
Hypercubic describes its product Hopper as an "agentic TN3270 terminal emulator" that uses AI agents to navigate and operate inside mainframe z/OS environments.
Hopper is designed for z/OS engineers to help them navigate ISPF, write column-strict JCL, debug failed jobs, and query VSAM datasets using AI agents in a modern development environment.

Hypercubic claims Hopper is the first agentic development environment for mainframes, combining TN3270 terminal, datasets and jobs browsers, and an AI agent capable of operating across multiple mainframe subsystems.
Hopper runs entirely on the user's laptop and connects to the mainframe over standard TN3270 and optional FTP protocols without requiring any installation on the mainframe itself.
Users can download Hopper for Windows, macOS, and Linux without needing to talk to the company first, including a free Hobby tier that requires no credit card.
Hopper depends on the existence of standard mainframe protocols TN3270 (required) and FTP (optional but recommended) to connect and operate within z/OS environments.
Hypercubic launched Hopper as of at least May 2026, publicly announcing it on Hacker News in May 2026.
Disqualifier D-1 — The team is named and nothing any of them is stated to have built appears in the evidence, and the company has no public repository.

what_would_change_my_mind.text: Disqualifier D-1: find a stated prior role for somebody they name, something one of them is stated to have built, or a public repository. It would then no longer hold, and the call would no longer be forced to Pass.
D1 Founder–market fit & technical depth: find a prior employer, role or period stated for somebody the company names. That moves it from 6–12 to 13–19 (+7).
D2 Wedge specificity: find a named customer, design partner or user, stated to be using it for that job. That moves it from 11–15 to 16–20 (+5).
